title: Architecture and Standards 2024 Unified Guidelines and ADRs
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Purpose and scope

This page consolidates Redwood Inference\u2019s architecture and standards across API design, coding practices, infrastructure/IaC, model-serving, observability, performance targets, and the Decision Record (ADR) process. The guidance below is normative for all services that serve customer-facing or platform-level inference traffic.

Audience
- Engineers (backend, infra, runtime)
- Product and platform owners implementing service-level changes
- SRE and reliability engineers
- Security & compliance reviewers

Principles (high-level)
1. Predictable: prioritize deterministic performance characteristics (latency, throughput) and clear SLAs.
2. Observable: every service must emit metrics, traces, and structured logs with correlation IDs.
3. Reversible: design changes to be rolled back or safely degraded (feature flags, model fallbacks).
4. Secure by default: least privilege, encrypted-in-transit and at-rest, key management.
5. Developer ergonomics: clear SDKs, consistent API semantics, straightforward local dev.

Sections
1) API standards
Intro: All public and internal REST endpoints must follow the API standard below. When deviating, you must open an ADR and list compatibility, migration plan, and rollout steps.

- Base style: JSON over HTTPS (TLS1.2+). Primary API surfaces: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank, /v1/health.
- Versioning:
  - Use major version in path: /v1/. Minor compatibility changes should be rolled out without changing the path if backward compatible. Breaking changes require a new major version and an ADR.
- Authentication: Bearer tokens (short-lived session tokens for web clients, long-lived service tokens for server-to-server). Enforce token scoping by route.
- Request/response shape:
  - Use explicit schemas (OpenAPI) stored in the repo: infra/api-schemas/openapi.yaml.
  - Responses must include a top-level "meta" object with request_id, model_version, and cost_estimate when applicable.
  - Example response header: {"request_id": "uuid", "x-model-version": "redwood-7b-v2" }
- Error handling:
  - Use HTTP status codes (4xx client, 5xx server). Return structured error body: {"error": {"code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED", "message": "Rate limit exceeded", "details": null}}
- Rate limiting and quotas:
  - Token-based rate limiting enforced at gateway. Default soft limits: 120 requests/minute per token; adjust per customer via product config.
- Pagination & streaming:
  - For large result sets use cursor-based pagination. Streaming endpoints (e.g., token streams) must support SSE/HTTP chunked responses with consistent chunk framing.
- Schema evolution:
  - Always add nullable fields rather than change type. Deprecation: mark fields deprecated in OpenAPI, keep compatibility for one major release cycle.

API Example (OpenAPI snippet recommended in repo):

  # Example: /v1/generate request
  POST /v1/generate
  Content-Type: application/json
  Authorization: Bearer <token>

  Request body:
  {
    "model": "redwood-7b-v2",
    "inputs": "Translate to French: Hello world",
    "parameters": {"max_tokens": 128, "temperature": 0.2}
  }

  Successful response:
  {
    "meta": {"request_id": "uuid-1234", "model_version": "redwood-7b-v2"},
    "output": "Bonjour le monde"
  }

2) Coding standards
- Languages: Go (services), Python (infra tooling, evals), TypeScript (console/frontend), Rust (performance-critical components).
- Linting and formatting:
  - Go: gofmt + golangci-lint with company preset.
  - Python: black + ruff; mypy for type checks.
  - TypeScript: eslint + prettier; tsconfig strict.
  - Rust: rustfmt + clippy.
- Code review:
  - Minimum two reviewers for service changes; at least one reviewer must be from the owning team.
  - All PRs must include unit and integration tests that run in CI.
- Testing:
  - Unit test coverage target: >= 60% for non-trivial services. Critical path components (inference routing, billing) should be >= 80%.
  - Include deterministic integration tests that can run in CI using small, mocked model containers.
- Dependency management:
  - Pin transitive deps in build manifests. Run dependency-scan tool and patch critical vulnerabilities within 7 days.

3) Infrastructure & IaC standards
- IaC: terraform for cloud infra; Helm charts for k8s manifests. Store modules in infra/terraform-modules.
- Environment separation: dev/staging/prod with separate cloud accounts and VPCs.
- Naming conventions: resource names must include team, env, service (e.g., r-inference-prod-redis-01).
- Networking:
  - Use private subnets for compute. Public endpoints only via API gateway with WAF.
- Secrets & keys:
  - Use central KMS/HSM integration; secrets not stored in plaintext in repo. Use secrets manager with RBAC.
- Deployment policies:
  - Blue/green or canary deploy for critical services; automated rollback on P95 latency regression or error budget burn > 25% in a 15-minute window.

Terraform module example (recommended settings)
- minimal example: 
  module "vpc" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@repo/infra/terraform-modules//vpc"
    env = "prod"
    owner = "eng-platform"
  }

4) Model-serving standards
- Packaging:
  - Use model bundles with manifest.yaml listing model id, architecture, tokenizer, quantization profile, supported sequence lengths, and signature for input/output schemas.
- Quantization profiles:
  - Store per-model packing profiles in confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles. Reference profiles by name in manifest.
- Runtime compatibility:
  - Runtime must advertise capabilities (e.g., fp32, int8, kv_cache_v2, grouped_attention) via a capabilities JSON at startup. The router should only route requests to compatible nodes; incompatible routes must trigger a graceful fallback.
- Caching and batching:
  - Automatic prefix caching enabled for chat sessions; default prefix cache TTL 10 minutes.
  - Batching: continuous batching with configurable max_batch_size and max_wait_ms. Default: max_batch_size=64, max_wait_ms=8.
- Model versioning & rollouts:
  - Version in manifest (semver-like). Rollouts require a canary slice (5% traffic for 1 hour), automated quality checks (synthetic prompt set), and a gradual ramp to 50% then 100% if no regressions. Document rollback criteria in the ADR.
- Quality and regression testing:
  - Every model checkout must run a regression suite (prompt set) comparing outputs to baseline; quality delta thresholds configured per task (default: semantic similarity decline > 3% triggers manual review).

Model manifest example (yaml recommended in repo):
  id: redwood-13b-v1
  architecture: transformer
  tokenizer: bpe-v2
  quantization_profile: int8-mixed
  max_sequence_length: 8192

5) Observability standards
- Metrics:
  - All services must emit Prometheus-style metrics with standardized labels: service, env, region, model_version, route.
  - Critical metrics (per-route): request_count, token_count, latency_p50, latency_p95, error_count, cache_hit_count.
- Tracing:
  - Use OpenTelemetry. Span must include request_id and model_version. Sampling: adaptive sampling configured at gateway; full traces for errors.
- Logs:
  - Structured JSON logs with level, timestamp, request_id, trace_id, and context. Avoid PII.
- Dashboards & runbooks:
  - Each service must have a perf dashboard and a runbook for the top 5 incidents (latency spike, OOM, degraded throughput, model failure, auth failure).
- Alerts and thresholds (example):
  - Paging alert: p95 latency > 2x baseline for 10 minutes or error_rate > 1% for 5 minutes.
  - Warning alert: sudden increase in token_count per request (possible abusive usage).

6) Performance standards and SLOs
- Global SLOs (platform-facing default):
  - Latency (text generation, per-request): p50 < 50ms, p95 < 350ms for small models (<=7B) under normal load. For large models (>7B) default: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 600ms.
  - Embeddings: p95 < 120ms.
  - Availability: 99.9% monthly uptime for hosted API routes (SLA-backed for paid customers is documented in product pages).
  - Throughput: dedicated pools should guarantee sustained throughput targets documented in Dedicated capacity contracts.
- Error budget policy:
  - Teams own error budgets per service. If error budget burn > 50% in a 7-day sliding window, the team must open an incident review and freeze non-critical feature launches.
- Benchmarking:
  - Use the internal benchmarking suite (eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite) to produce reproducible latency/throughput numbers. All model onboarding must include a benchmark report.

7) Decision Records (ADRs) process
- Purpose: ADRs capture architectural decisions that have long-term consequences. Every breaking or cross-cutting change must have an ADR.
- Format: Use template ADR-YYYYMMDD-<short-title>.md stored in docs/adr. Required fields: status, context, decision, consequences, owners, date.
- Review: ADRs affecting multiple teams must be reviewed by affected owners and at least one engineering manager from platform.
- Index: Maintain an ADR index table on this page and in docs/adr/INDEX.md.

Sample ADR index (short form)
- ADR-20240115-scheduling-kernel: Adopt Kahn-style scheduler for KV cache eviction; owner: eng-serving-runtime; status: accepted; link: docs/adr/ADR-20240115-scheduling-kernel.md
- ADR-20240302-api-versioning: Major-path versioning for public APIs; owner: eng-developer-experience; status: accepted; link: docs/adr/ADR-20240302-api-versioning.md
- ADR-20240610-quantization-defaults: Default to mixed-int8 quantization for 7B models in Dedicated; owner: applied-ml; status: in_review; link: docs/adr/ADR-20240610-quantization-defaults.md

Operational runbook excerpt: High latency on /v1/generate
1. Triage: Check global dashboard > route filters > p95 latency and request rate.
2. Identify scope: Is impact per-customer or global? Check traffic slices and model_version tag.
3. Hot fixes (in order):
   a. Increase serving pool capacity (scale up dedicated nodes) if autoscaler not responding.
   b. Route traffic to fallback model variant (configured in smart routing).
   c. Disable experimental features (structured prompting, reranking) via feature flag.
4. If degraded > 30 minutes: open outage and notify Cx via standard template.
5. Postmortem: run the regression-triage template and attach benchmark artifacts.

Ownership matrix (high-level)
- API standards: eng-developer-experience
- Coding standards: eng-developer-experience + eng-platform
- Infra/IaC: eng-infra
- Model-serving runtime: eng-serving-runtime + applied-ml-and-evals
- Observability: eng-platform + eng-sre
- Performance & benchmarking: eng-serving-runtime

Governance and change process
- Minor changes: documented in this page and a short RFC in team repo; reviewers: owners list.
- Major/breaking changes: ADR required, cross-team signoff, canary plan, and rollback criteria documented.
- Periodic review: This document and related ADR index reviewed quarterly by owners.

Appendices
A. Useful commands and snippets
- Collect a trace (OTel collector CLI): otel-cli record --service redwood-api --output trace.json --duration 30s
- Run local inference smoke test (docker): docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 redwood/local-model:latest \n  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"local-test","inputs":"Hello"}'

B. Templates and links
- ADR template: docs/adr/TEMPLATE.md
- OpenAPI schemas: infra/api-schemas/openapi.yaml
- Quantization profiles: confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles
- Benchmarking harness: eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite

Change log
- 2024-05-10: Created (A. Martinez)
- 2025-02-12: Added default batching/wait_ms guidance and rollout canary steps (R. Patel)
- 2026-03-01: Updated SLOs for small and large models; clarified metrics labels and alert thresholds (S. Gomez)

Contact and escalation
- For questions about these standards open an RFC in the owning team's repo or contact owners listed in the Ownership matrix. For urgent incidents, follow oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process.
